## A polynomial extrapolation

### Problem
The monic polynomial $f(x)$ has degree 9, and $f(n) = n$ for each integer $n$, $1 \le n \le 9$. Find $f(10)$, and justify your answer. ("Monic" means with leading coefficient 1.)

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
We show that $f(10) = 9! + 10 = 362890$.

Let $g(x) = f(x) - x$. Since $f(x)$ has degree 9 and leading coefficient 1, $g(x)$ is also monic of degree 9.

Furthermore, for $n = 1, 2, \dots, 9$,

$$g(n) = f(n) - n = 0.$$

Therefore $1, 2, \dots, 9$ are the 9 roots of $g(x)$, so

$$g(x) = (x - 1)(x - 2) \cdots (x - 9).$$

Evaluating at $x = 10$:

$$g(10) = (10 - 1)(10 - 2) \cdots (10 - 9) = 9 \cdot 8 \cdots 1 = 9! = 362880.$$

Hence

$$f(10) = g(10) + 10 = 9! + 10 = 362890.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
The difference $g(x) = f(x) - x$ vanishes at 9 distinct points. Because $\deg(g) = 9$ and $g$ is monic, it is uniquely determined by its linear factors. Evaluating at 10 gives $g(10) = 9!$, so $f(10) = 9! + 10 = 362890$.

### Key Technique
Defining the difference polynomial $g(x) = f(x) - x$ and factoring monic polynomials with known integer roots.
